additional_considerations.rationale: Often follows strenuous or unusual exertion with paraspinal tenderness, but the pain usually does not radiate to the extremities.
Common; pain is typically worse with activity and better with rest, and radicular symptoms may be present.
Patients are typically over 50 and back or bone pain may be the only complaint; anemia, neuropathy, hypercalcemia and renal failure are also common.
Intentional faking of symptoms for secondary gain, such as getting out of work.

source_issues: e006: 'Babinski sign bilaterally' gives no direction (upgoing/downgoing); recorded as 'Result not documented' with a flag (x010). The SP is told to show normal reflexes.
e006: 'Straight leg raising is 80 degrees bilaterally' does not say whether the maneuver reproduced pain; the angle is kept and the missing pain response is flagged (x013).
e002 'VS: Within Normal Limits' disagrees with the doorway heart rate of 50/minute (below the usual normal range).
Alcohol: script says 'a few beers on the weekends'; the note says '1-2 beers on weekends'.
Note SH says 'CAGE 0/4', but the script asks only the Cut-down question (p023).

Note HPI says the 1-year intermittent pain 'is relieved by lying down after ambulation'; the script (p016) says it goes away when he stops walking and sits down (gold #2 also says 'resolves with sitting'). The note also says 'worsens with movement' where the script says walking, sitting for a long time and coughing.
Note FH 'Noncontributory', although the script gives father's death from a heart attack at 65.
p024 and p025 questions carry stray quotation marks ('"Have you ever used illegal substances?', '"Do you smoke'') from the raw sheet.
The SP sheet's patient description says he lives with his girlfriend; this is not in any Q/A or the note and has no valid source id.
annotator_notes: Per a later policy update (which overrides the GUIDE.md Babinski example wording), env findings carry no review commentary: an undirected Babinski is recorded as 'Result not documented' and the reason is in the record's flags.

The current pain (1 week, after lifting) is 'current'; the year-long on-and-off back and leg pain with walking (p016) is 'recurrent' and kept separate, because the two pains have different triggers and relief.

Urinary straining and incomplete emptying are coded as ROS (not the presenting complaint). The 6-month duration is attached only to straining, as stated; incomplete emptying is 'sometimes' with no duration (the note gives 6 months for both).
'Lives with his girlfriend' is placed in persona.acting_notes as background, because patient facts need a Q/A, cc or note source.
Behavioral SP instructions that describe examinable findings (tenderness, normal neuro findings, forward lean) are also added as sp_notes exam records (x015-x019).
